chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, raising it, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when his son-in-law came to him (either as the husband of his daughter or his sister), would spread his cloak for him, then seat him, then say: 'Welcome to the one who suffices the needs and veils the privacy'.
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette for receiving a son-in-law in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) demonstrates the ideal etiquette of the *Khal* (son-in-law) by personally spreading his cloak for his guest, symbolizing honor and intimacy. The greeting 'May Allah suffice you with provision and cover your nakedness' underscores the spiritual and social weight of marriage as a means of securing familial stability and dignity, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights and status of in-laws.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, raising it, said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> would spread his<sup>asws</sup> own gown as a furnishing when a husband of his daughter or sister would come (to see him) and  then would make him to be seated, then he<sup>asws</sup> would be saying: ‘Welcome to the one who suffices the needs and veils the privacy’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from Nuh ibn Shu’ayb in a marfu’ manner who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would spread his gown as furnishing when the husband of his daughter or sister would come to him (the Imam) and would say, ‘Welcome to the one who has taken good care of a need and the one who protected the privacy.’”
